markdown: ## Watchlist - **UniCredit:** An Irish Times commentary says "Italian wile trumps German ineptitude" in securing the Commerzbank deal [The Irish Times](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxQQms0NnlCaFIweVc4aXVUZnctdEtLWlB0Ymd2UENiZGdFY1VZMkdIRThqeHlFbnpseEVpbDRLeG00OHlwSzM3VFg1enduQ3k4TGE0UGMwb0pmMHdpWnN1X0Z5QkxpVjJUa0VZdmN1dUprdkdpOGg3QjJnSGhRelVQRm1aSXJHdDFLNGNLQ3lrUEd5aXpqMXROdWZtOHFmZHZrY2l6RWd4N3hrTGpNNnBQaXR3?oc=5). With the takeover settled, plan for the combined UniCredit–Commerzbank relationship in 2027, including counterparty limits and platform changes. ## The brief - **Bill has agreed to be acquired for $6bn by TPG in partnership with Corpay** [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/111752/bill-agrees-to-be-acquired-by-tpg-in-6bn-deal?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed)[Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/bill-sells-for-6b-to-tpg-corpay/875331/). The deal fuels consolidation in business payments and receivables software. If Carrier uses Bill or Corpay for payables or cards, expect roadmap and pricing changes, so review the contract terms and data portability. - **Traders are starting to move US copper to China as fears of Trump tariffs ease** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/b84dbcb1-f216-422e-89c7-f203e0ab2757?syn-25a6b1a6=1). An acute Chinese shortage and a high local premium have created a lucrative arbitrage. Copper is a key HVAC input, so watch for upward pressure on US copper prices and review metal hedges and supplier pricing clauses. - **US-China trade, Taiwan and tech tensions remain unresolved after the APEC meetings in Shenzhen** [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/apec-summit-trump-xi-china-trade-taiwan.html). Analysts note few concrete outcomes, so keep tariff and China-sourcing scenarios live in the 2027 plan rather than assuming a deal. - **US ports face an onslaught of cyber attacks as hackers target vital trade routes** [Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/c269cf3e-2275-4244-9a86-f412c8521b4f?syn-25a6b1a6=1). America's biggest crude oil export hub reports thousands of attempted hacks each day. Port disruption could delay inbound components, so check how much inventory buffer and alternate routing the supply chain has. ## Rates & FX - **Treasuries rallied hard.** The 2-year fell 13bp to 4.63% (-25bp on the week) and the 10-year fell 12bp to 4.92% (-23bp), back below 5%. It may be a window to lock in term funding or extend investment duration. SOFR is 3.91%. - **The peso keeps sliding.** USD/MXN rose 0.79% to 19.067, up 2.55% on the week. Mexican costs are cheaper in dollars, so consider extending peso cost hedges at these levels. - **Other currencies.** The yen firmed, with USD/JPY down 0.83% to 158.64. EUR/USD is 1.0990, GBP/USD is 1.3125 and EUR/GBP is 0.8374. USD/CNY rose 0.16% to 6.6777. €STR is 2.441% and SONIA is 3.984%. - **No high-impact data today.** US core PCE (forecast +0.3%) and preliminary Q3 GDP (forecast 3.5%) are due on Wednesday at 13:30 Dublin. Lagarde's latest speech is titled "Acting in time" [ECB](https://www.ecb.europa.eu//press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp261120~e52bcc4db2.en.html), and Warsh wants Fed officials to talk less, though they are talking more [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/warsh-fed-forward-guidance-rate-hikes.html). ## Also worth knowing - **Worldline shares fell as much as 20% after the FT reported it delayed supplier payments and sought cash advances from customers** [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48791/worldline-shares-plummet-on-ft-report-on-cash-advances?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed). - **UK SME lender OakNorth has won a US national bank charter, the first foreign digital bank to do so** [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/oaknorth-fed-occ-approve-charter-application-michigan-bank-acquisition-digital-uk/875357/). - **Textron is selling its industrial business to a private equity buyer for $1.2bn** to become a pure-play aerospace and defence company [Manufacturing Dive](https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/textron-selling-specialized-vehicles-kautex-kingswood-capital-management/875269/). - **PayPal has named Claire Bramley as CFO from February**, as Jamie Miller leaves in a team overhaul [Finextra](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/111755/paypal-names-claire-bramley-cfo?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed)[Payments Dive](https://www.paymentsdive.com/news/paypal-ceo-remakes-team/875344/). ## Worth thinking about HBR argues that recent technology breakdowns show organisations aren't spending enough time stress-testing their operations [HBR](/2026/11/were-seeing-the-costs-of-moving-fast). Meanwhile, banks are racing to patch vulnerabilities as AI speeds up attackers [Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/banks-patching-vulnerabilities-tech-outage-risk-ai-cybersecurity/875329/). When did treasury last run a full drill of a bank, TMS or payment-network outage, and what did it reveal?
